_comment: UAply help articles. The assistant answers only from these, and shows which article it used. Keep each body short, true to the app, and in plain language. 'tags' are extra words people might type. 'go' is the app screen the article is about (section:item) and becomes a button in the chat. An article may carry a 'release' object used by the release build (dev): {'body': replacement text} or {'hide': true}.

articles.title: What is UAply?
articles.tags: about app how it works swipe start begin new
articles.body: UAply shows you one job at a time. Swipe right (or tap Apply) to apply, swipe left (or tap Pass) to skip. Each card shows a match percentage that compares the job with your profile, so finish Profile setup first to get accurate matches.

articles.title: How do I apply to a job? (What happens when I swipe right)
articles.tags: how to apply apply applying application send submit employer recruiter swipe right undo consent
articles.body: Swiping right applies for you. The first time, UAply explains what is sent and asks you to agree. If the employer has agreed to receive applications through UAply, your profile details are sent to them. Otherwise UAply opens the employer's own application page so you can finish there. Every application is saved in Dashboard, Applied, and you can tap Undo right after a swipe. In this test version, applications go to a test inbox and nothing reaches a real company.

release.body: Swiping right applies for you. The first time, UAply explains what is sent and asks you to agree. If the employer has agreed to receive applications through UAply (the card says Apply instantly), your profile details are sent to them. For every other job (the card says Opens employer site) nothing is sent: the job is kept in Dashboard, Applied as Not sent yet, and Finish now opens the employer's own application page so you can finish there. You can tap Undo right after a swipe.

articles.title: How is the match percentage worked out?
articles.tags: match score percent percentage compatibility points why low
articles.body: The match is a fixed formula, not a judgment about you. It adds points for skills (30), experience (15), pay (15), job title (15), work style (10), location (10) and education (5). Each card lists the points for every part. Skills also count when your headline, About you or major says them, and the card tells you how many came from there. If you tick no work style, every style scores full points. The score only orders jobs for you. It never rejects you and never decides anything about hiring. Improve it by completing your profile and target titles.

articles.title: How do I set up my profile?
articles.tags: profile settings name email phone setup fill in details complete readiness
articles.body: Open Profile, then Profile setup. It is five short steps: About you, Jobs you want, Where and pay, Background and links, and Eligibility and extras. Tap Save and continue on each step; your answers are saved as you go and you can jump between steps any time. The bar at the top shows how complete your profile is. On a computer, a card beside the questions shows what employers will see. Your profile is what employers receive when you apply.

articles.title: What are target titles?
articles.tags: title titles job title role position target sales hide coding wrong jobs
articles.body: Target titles are the job names you want, up to five (for example Account Executive, Inside Sales Representative, Closer). Add them in Profile setup, under Jobs you want. Jobs whose role name matches score higher, and jobs that don't match are hidden so you only see roles you would accept. Common equivalents count, like developer and engineer. To see everything, turn off 'Hide roles that do not match my target titles' in Profile, Filters.

articles.title: Adding skills
articles.tags: skills skill add typo spelling limit maximum suggestions
articles.body: In Profile setup, under Jobs you want, start typing a skill and pick it from the suggestion list to avoid typos. UAply also warns you about likely misspellings. You can add up to 25 skills. A skill your headline, About you or major already mentions counts too.

articles.title: Why don't I see any jobs (or only a few)?
articles.tags: no jobs empty nothing few listings missing where jobs come from source feed
articles.body: Three things can hide jobs. Your filters (Profile, Filters) may be too strict: try Clear all filters. Your target titles hide roles that don't match: add more titles or turn that filter off. And UAply currently lists jobs from employers that agreed to work with it, plus example listings, so there are not many real openings yet. More employers are being added.

release.body: Three things can hide jobs. Your filters (Profile, Filters) may be too strict: try Clear all filters. Your target titles hide roles that don't match: add more titles or turn that filter off. And UAply lists real postings from employers' own public career pages, so the mix changes as employers add and remove openings. Most listings are full-time jobs and internships; part-time and Coop roles are rare, so those lists can be short or empty.

articles.title: How do filters work?
articles.tags: filter filters posted date recent 24 hours week month applicants under 10 benefits experience level commission companies keywords minimum match
articles.body: Open Profile, then Filters. You can show jobs posted in the past 24 hours, week or month, jobs with under 10 applicants, jobs that mention benefits you pick, experience levels, and a minimum match. You can hide work styles you did not pick, jobs that pay below your minimum, jobs that need more education than you have, companies, and keywords. If your titles are in sales, you can also remove commission-only roles. Some listings don't say everything; turn on 'Hide listings that do not say' to hide those too. Clear all filters resets them.

articles.title: Where is the distance filter?
articles.tags: distance miles radius near me close commute location city 10 20 50
articles.body: Open Profile, then Filters, and drag the Commute distance slider. Far left shows remote jobs only, and far right shows every job. In between you choose how many miles from you in-person jobs can be, from 5 to 100. UAply measures from your device location if you tapped Use my location, otherwise from your city or ZIP code.

release.body: Distance is in Profile setup, under Where and pay, and it only appears when you tick Hybrid or On-site under work style, because remote jobs don't need it. Choose 10, 20, 50 or 100 miles from where you live. UAply finds that from your city and state, or from your ZIP code if it doesn't know the city. Distance works for most larger US cities.

articles.title: Full-time, part-time, internships and Coop
articles.tags: services full-time part-time internship internships co-op coop job type
articles.body: Tap Services at the bottom to switch between Full-time, Part-time, Internships and Coop. Each one has its own stack of jobs. The types you tick in Profile setup, under Jobs you want, open first.

articles.title: Adding my resume
articles.tags: resume cv upload file pdf word link document
articles.body: Open Profile, then Profile setup, step 4 (Background and links). Upload your resume file (PDF, Word or text, up to 1 MB), or add a link to it, such as a Google Drive link anyone can open. The file is saved on your device and goes along with each application UAply sends to an employer; UAply's server does not keep a copy. For jobs you finish on the employer's own site, upload it there. To fill in your profile from it, choose your resume under Fill from your resume at the top of that step: UAply fills in the fields that are still empty, never changes what you typed (it offers Replace where your resume differs), and shows the line each answer came from so you can check it. The file is read on UAply's server for a moment and not kept.

release.body: Open Profile, then Profile setup, step 4 (Background and links). Upload your resume file (PDF, Word or text, up to 1 MB), or add a link to it, such as a Google Drive link anyone can open. The file is saved on your device and goes along with each application UAply sends to an employer; UAply's server does not keep a copy. For jobs you finish on the employer's own site, upload it there.

articles.title: Tracking my applications
articles.tags: dashboard track tracking applied interview interviews accepted offer rejected status follow up calendar export csv
articles.body: Dashboard shows everything you applied to. Overview gives totals and what's coming up. Move an application to Interview, Accepted or Rejected with its buttons, and tap Details to add an interview time, an offer, a reason or notes. Interviews can be added to your calendar, and you can export everything as a spreadsheet (CSV).

articles.title: Accounts, signing in and email receipts
articles.tags: account sign in sign up log in login create password email receipt confirmation google apple
articles.body: Tap Sign in at the top right to create an account with your email and a password. You must be 18 or older. Once you are signed in and have confirmed your email with the 6-digit code, every swipe right sends a receipt to your email. Google sign-in appears when it has been switched on for this server. Apple, phone and email-link sign-in are not available yet.

articles.title: I forgot my password
articles.tags: forgot password reset change locked out can't log in
articles.body: Open Profile, then Account, tap I already have an account, then Forgot password?. Enter your account email and UAply emails you a link that works for one hour. Open it and choose a new password; that signs you out on every device, so log in again with the new password. If no email arrives, check spam, then use Talk to a person. After too many wrong tries, wait a few minutes before trying again.

articles.title: Deleting my account or my data
articles.tags: delete remove account data erase privacy close cancel account
articles.body: To delete your account, open Profile, then Account, scroll to the bottom and open More account options, then tap Delete my account. You'll be offered a short, anonymous survey (you can skip it), then asked for your password and to confirm. That removes your receipts and application records from UAply's server and can't be undone. To erase what is saved on this device, open Profile, then Data and privacy, and use Delete all my data.

articles.title: Voluntary questions (race, gender, veteran, disability)
articles.tags: voluntary eeo race ethnicity gender veteran disability hispanic self identification demographic why
articles.body: Many employers ask these on their forms, so UAply lets you record your answers once in Profile setup, in the optional section on the last step. Every question is optional and has Prefer not to say. Your answers stay on your device, are never used to score or filter jobs, and are never sent automatically. They only leave your device if you tap Copy my answers and paste them yourself.

articles.title: Work authorization and sponsorship
articles.tags: work authorization visa sponsorship citizen green card opt h1b permit
articles.body: You can record whether you are authorized to work in the US and whether you will need visa sponsorship. These are optional, are used only to fill in applications, and never affect your match. UAply can't give immigration advice; for that, talk to an immigration attorney.

articles.title: Messaging the hiring manager
articles.tags: message hiring manager recruiter note cover letter personalized plus pro
articles.body: On Plus and Pro, you can turn on 'Message the hiring manager' in Profile setup, on the last step. It adds a short message, filled in from your profile and the job, to each application. It is off until you turn it on, and it only goes to employers that accept applications through UAply.

release.body: In Profile setup, on the last step, you can turn on 'Message the hiring manager'. It adds a short message, filled in from your profile and the job, to each application. It is off until you turn it on, and it only goes to employers that accept applications through UAply.

articles.title: Plans and billing
articles.tags: plan plans billing price cost pay subscription free plus pro upgrade cancel refund limit weekly applications many
articles.body: There are three plans. Free: 50 applications a week. Plus ($9.99 a month): 250 a week, plus extra filters and Message the hiring manager. Pro ($19.99 a month): unlimited applications. Limits count the last 7 days. Open Profile, then Plan and billing to see your usage, switch or cancel. In this test version no real payments are taken: choosing a plan only records a test payment and no card is ever asked for.

release.body: Open Profile, then Plan and billing. While it says paid plans are coming, UAply is free during early access: no weekly limit on applications, every filter and Message the hiring manager are included, and nothing is charged. When paid plans start, the page shows Free (50 applications a week), Plus ($9.99 a month, 250 a week) and Pro ($19.99 a month, unlimited). You need an account to choose one, payment is made on Stripe's own secure page so UAply never sees your card number, and you can cancel any time in Manage billing.

articles.title: What data does UAply keep, and does it sell my data?
articles.tags: privacy data personal information stored keep share sell sold selling sells cookies
articles.body: Your profile is saved on your device. Each time you swipe right, UAply's server keeps a record of that application (the job and the details sent with it) so it can deliver it and show what happened. If you create an account, your email, a scrambled form of your password and your receipts are kept too; deleting your account removes them and the applications you made while signed in. Employers only receive your details when you apply to one that agreed to receive applications. UAply does not sell your information. The Privacy Policy, linked at the bottom of the app, has the details.

articles.title: About this assistant: is it AI or a real person?
articles.tags: assistant bot chatbot ai artificial intelligence human real person who are you
articles.body: This assistant is automated, not a person, and it can make mistakes. It answers from UAply's help articles and cannot see your profile, applications or account. Please don't type passwords or sensitive personal details. Tap Talk to a person to reach the UAply team.

articles.title: Talk to a person
articles.tags: human person agent support contact email help team call
articles.body: Tap Talk to a person in this chat to email the UAply team, or leave a message here with your email and someone will get back to you. You can also email uaplytechnologies@uaply.net; the Support page (linked at the bottom of the app) says what to include, and we usually reply within 2 business days.

articles.title: Giving feedback or reporting a problem
articles.tags: feedback suggestion idea bug problem broken report issue complaint
articles.body: Tap Give feedback or Report a problem in this chat. It takes about 30 seconds, and a person on the UAply team reads every message.

articles.title: Why do I need to verify my email?
articles.tags: verify verification code email confirm 6 digit code not received spam resend identity
articles.body: When you make an account with an email and password, UAply emails you a 6-digit code. Enter it under Profile, Account to prove the email is really yours. The code works for 10 minutes and 5 tries; tap Send a new code if it expires or you cannot find it (check spam). Until you verify, you can still swipe, but you will not get confirmation emails and cannot apply directly to employers. If you sign in with Google, your email is already verified.

articles.title: Signing in with Google
articles.tags: google gmail sign in continue with google account password saved browser login
articles.body: Tap Continue with Google under Profile, Account. Google shows the accounts already signed in on your browser, and you pick one. UAply never sees your Google password, only your verified email address. If you already made a UAply account with the same email and a password, Google signs you into that same account. Use the same way to sign in each time. You can also sign in with any email and a password; UAply then checks the email with a 6-digit code.
